Job Description

Background

While climate change is observed across Nepal, the rate of temperature increase is more pronounced at higher altitudes. This temperature rise accelerates the rate of glacial retreat, increasing the size of glacial lakes located in these high-altitude areas and, in turn, their likelihood of breaching in the form of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF) which cause severe flooding, landslides and mudflows that damage infrastructure and private assets, and disrupt transportation networks, agricultural production, power supplies from hydropower plants and tourism activities. Damages from GLOFs are often irreparable for decades, with considerable economic costs, particularly to downstream populations. The risk of GLOFs is further exacerbated by increasing temperatures which increase the rate of snow and ice melt and the proportion of precipitation falling as rain, which increases the volume of the lakes, thereby reducing the amount of ‘freeboard’, which increases the likelihood of overflow and the intensity of resulting floods.

The Thulagi, Lower Barun, Lumding Tsho and Hongu 2 Lakes are at exceptionally high risk of breaching having already exhibited considerable increases in volume, accelerated degradation of their ice-cored moraines, and a reduced amount of ‘freeboard’ as a result of climate change. Combined, these factors have destabilized the lakes, exposing the Gandaki Basin and the Dudhkoshi and Arun Sub-basins to the threat of a GLOF event. Without intervention, these glacial lakes could breach at any given moment, adversely impacting vulnerable Nepalese communities.

In response to this risk, USD36 millions of GCF funds, alongside USD14 million in cofinance, will be directed to reduce the risk and impacts of GLOFs at the four priority glacial lakes by shifting towards a proactive approach to GLOF risk reduction in Nepal. The proposed project presents an integrated approach to GLOF risk management in Nepal by addressing institutional and technical capacities, physical protection (both grey and green infrastructure approaches), hazard monitoring and early warning. This integrated approach will utilise GCF funds to: i) lower the water levels of four glacial lakes to reduce their risk of breaching; ii) implement Eco-Disaster Risk Reduction interventions in mountain ecosystems to mitigate the residual flood impacts from a GLOF; iii) establish and implement early warning systems to alleviate damages and prevent the loss of lives from GLOFs; and iv) strengthen the technical and institutional capacity of Nepal’s Department of Hydrology and Meteorology to plan for and respond to GLOFs and floods. These interventions will catalyse a shift from a need- and project-based approach towards proactive and pre-emptive approaches, engendered through strengthened capacity among institutions and communities.

The project will be implemented following UNDP’s support to National Implementation Modality (NIM), with Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) under Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation (MoEWRI) of Nepal serving as the Implementing Partner. Under this modality, UNDP is supporting DHM in recruiting key positions for the establishment of a Project Management Unit, which will be based in Kathmandu, Nepal. Members of the PMU will collectively be responsible for overall planning and budgeting, collaborating with other ministries, sectors and government entities to implement the project performance management system; bidding for the provision of project consultancy services; coordination with the responsible parties in terms of bidding of goods and services; disbursement and implementation of project audits, operation of accounts, monitoring and preparation of overall project reports (annual), and safeguards policy monitoring reports.

Updating the rates of the commodities which are buying on daily basis.
Asking for and updating the rates of other edible goods from various parties.Finding new vendors / new products.
Preparation of Import chart (LC wise) and updating the same on weekly basis and providing the hard copy to the director every Friday.

Preparation and updating of LC wise chart once a week and Insurance claim sheet and debit note against weight shortage.

Monthly analysis of commodity goods, landing price & proper analysis to be done in terms of expected buying price & daily sales prices. 
Preparation of Sales Order in the absence of concerned staff.

Experience in edible oil or commodity trading industry 
Knowledge of Nepal–India import regulations 
Ability to handle multiple consignments simultaneously 
Strong coordination skills with logistics partners 
3years of experience in procurement, imports, or commodity trading 
Hands-on experience with: LC documentation and import coordination 
Experience dealing with Clearing & Forwarding agents, preferably Kolkata route.

title: Sales Consultant (Request for Proposal)
description:
About the job

Request for Proposal 




Title: Sales Consultant

Issued by: Aloi Private Limited 

Issued Date: 27 January 2026 

Initial Pilot Duration: 1 month (8 hours total) with potential scale-up 

Extended Engagement (if scaled): Up to 20 days per year 

Application Deadline: 6th February 2026 (Friday)




1. Background 




Aloi Private Limited works to enable inclusive access to finance and digital solutions across value chains in Nepal, with a strong focus on agriculture and dairy cooperatives. Through its digital platform and partnerships with financial institutions, Aloi supports dairy cooperatives and farmers to improve access to credit, strengthen operations, and enhance long-term sustainability. 




As Aloi deepens its engagement in the dairy value chain, it has identified a critical need to strengthen practical, on-ground sales capability within its internal teams. While strategic advisory support is important, Aloi’s immediate priority is to embed learning through real sales conversations with dairy cooperatives, supported by an experienced professional who can lead from the front and gradually transition into a structured consultant role. 




To address this, Aloi is seeking a consultant who can begin with direct involvement in sales calls and cooperative conversations, while simultaneously coaching the Aloi team to independently lead these engagements over time. 




2. Core Engagement Philosophy 

This assignment is intentionally designed as a sales-led, learn-by-doing engagement, not a traditional desk-based consultancy. 

The consultant is expected to: 

Start with hands-on sales involvement, including making or leading calls with dairy cooperatives 
Use live conversations as training moments for Aloi’s sales and field teams 
Gradually shift from being the primary caller to a guiding and mentoring role, enabling Aloi’s team to confidently lead discussions 
Package strategic guidance together with warm introductions, real negotiations, and practical follow-ups 




The focus is on how conversations are led, how value is articulated, and how trust with cooperatives is built and sustained. 




3. Scope of Work 

The scope is divided into two linked phases: an initial 1-month intensive pilot and a potential extended engagement based on performance and fit. 




3.1 Phase 1: Sales-Led Pilot Engagement (1 Month | 8 Hours Total) 

During the pilot month, the consultant will work closely with Aloi’s sales and product teams using a structured weekly format: 

Weekly Time Commitment (Approx. 2 hours per week): 

1 hour per week – Team Coaching & Review Call 
Review recent sales conversations and cooperative feedback 
Break down what worked, what did not, and why 
Improve pitching structure, confidence, and objection handling 
Prepare for upcoming cooperative calls 
1 hour per week – Live Cooperative Sales Calls (any of the following formats): 
Consultant leads calls directly with dairy cooperatives, with Aloi team observing 
Consultant makes calls jointly with Aloi team members 
Consultant facilitates calls while Aloi team members lead, with live guidance and post-call feedback 

The intent is to ensure that Aloi’s team learns by watching, participating, and gradually leading. 




At the end of the pilot month, Aloi and the consultant will jointly review: 

Team readiness and confidence improvement 
Effectiveness of the live-call learning approach 
Fit for scaling the engagement into a longer-term advisory role 




3.2 Phase 2: Transition to Structured Consultant Role 

If the pilot engagement is successful, the consultant’s role will gradually shift from direct sales execution to a more structured advisory and capacity-building role, while still retaining selective involvement in strategic conversations. 




Key areas include: 

a) Refinement of Sales Pitch and Engagement Framework 

Translate learnings from live calls into: 
Clear pitching flows 
Objection-handling guides 
Cooperative-specific value narratives 
Develop differentiated approaches for: 
Small vs. mature dairy cooperatives 
Individual cooperatives vs. clusters, unions, or federations 




b) Team Capacity Building 

Coach Aloi’s sales and field teams to independently: 
Lead cooperative conversations 
Manage follow-ups and next steps 
Maintain long-term cooperative relationships 
Support the development of simple playbooks and call structures 




c) Strategic Advisory & Warm Introductions 

Provide warm introductions to relevant cooperatives or sector actors, where feasible 
Advise Aloi on positioning, sequencing of outreach, and engagement strategy 
Support internal reflection on which cooperative segments to prioritise 




4. Key Deliverables 

Expected deliverables across the engagement include: 

Live, hands-on sales calls conducted with or in front of Aloi’s team 
Improved confidence and structure in Aloi team-led cooperative conversations 
Practical call scripts, pitch flows, and objection-handling notes 
Coaching sessions with clear, actionable feedback 
Short notes capturing learnings from sales conversations 
Recommendations on transitioning from supported to independent sales engagement 




5. Duration and Level of Effort 

Pilot Phase: 1 month, approximately 8 hours total 
If Extended: Up to 20 days per year 
Modality: Primarily remote calls, with selective in-person engagement if required 




6. Consultant Profile and Qualifications 

The consultant should have: 

Strong hands-on experience in selling to or engaging dairy cooperatives in Nepal 
Deep understanding of cooperative decision-making dynamics 
Proven ability to lead sales conversations, not just advise on them 
Experience coaching teams through live, practical engagement 
Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage sales environments 
Ability to transition from executor to mentor as team capacity improves 




7. Proposal Submission Requirements 

Interested consultants are requested to submit: 

A short technical proposal covering: 
Understanding of the sales-led engagement model 
Proposed approach for the 1-month pilot 
Relevant hands-on sales experience 
A financial proposal (hourly or daily rate) 
Updated CV highlighting relevant assignments 




8. Evaluation Criteria 

Proposals will be evaluated based on: 

Demonstrated hands-on sales experience with cooperatives 
Practicality of the proposed learning-by-doing approach 
Ability to coach while executing 
Clarity on transitioning from direct sales to advisory role 
Cost-effectiveness and availability 




9. Reporting and Coordination 

The consultant will work closely with Aloi’s designated focal person and relevant internal teams. Weekly check-ins will be used to review calls, progress, and learning outcomes, especially during the pilot phase. 




Interested individuals can send us their proposal and CV at careers@aloi.global by 6th February 2026.
